summary: Design standards, mockups and assets through Design Tools.

help:
Usage: st design [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Design Ops: UI mockups (hand-authored or AI) and game/marketing assets. Run
  `st design` for the full subcommand matrix.

Options:
  --install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
  --show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or
                        customize the installation.
  --help                Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  asset  Asset Studio: import self/user-generated images, generate game /...
  ui     UI Design mockups.
help.asset:
Usage: st design asset [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Asset Studio: import self/user-generated images, generate game / marketing
  artwork via Agent Hub image agents, and export sprite sheets. Ask the source
  gate first: manual/current-agent or Agent Hub? Storage must be durable;
  never /tmp.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  generate  Fallback Agent Hub image generation for callers with no...
  import    Import a self/user-generated image into Asset Studio for...
  critique  Critique a visual game asset through Agent Hub.
  export    Export an existing Design Ops asset.
help.asset generate:
Usage: st design asset generate [OPTIONS] {name} {prompt}

  Fallback Agent Hub image generation for callers with no native imagegen.

  Default rule: use the calling agent's native image generator first, save the
  result durably, then run `st design asset import` so Asset Studio still owns
  review/approval. This command is only for agents/surfaces with no native
  image generation; pass `--agent-hub-fallback` to confirm that.

  For hand-authored UI HTML, use `st design ui create` / `attach`. For AI-
  generated UI mockups from a live URL, use `st design ui analyze`.

Arguments:
  name    Asset display name  [required]
  prompt  Creative brief for the generated asset  [required]

Options:
  -d, --description <str>       Optional description stored with the asset
  -t, --type <str>              Asset type (sprite, sprite_sheet, portrait,
                                environment, icon, illustration, ui_texture,
                                marketing_mockup, tile_set, concept_art)
                                [default: sprite]
  -w, --workflow <str>          Workflow lane: concept, production, marketing,
                                ui  [default: concept]
  --size <str>                  Target size in WIDTHxHEIGHT format  [default:
                                1024x1024]
  --agent <str>                 Agent Hub image agent slug
  --style <str>                 Style direction for the image prompt
  --negative <str>              Negative prompt guidance
  --background <str>            Background mode: transparent, solid, scene
                                [default: transparent]
  --variants <int range>        Number of variants to generate  [default: 1;
                                1<=x<=4]
  --tags <str>                  Comma-separated tags
  --sheet-columns <int>         Sprite sheet columns
  --sheet-rows <int>            Sprite sheet rows
  --frame-width <int>           Sprite sheet frame width
  --frame-height <int>          Sprite sheet frame height
  --animations <str>            Comma-separated animation row labels
  --source-asset-id <int>       Source asset DB id for variant derivation
  --reference-image-path <str>  Path to a PNG/JPEG/WebP reference image for
                                sprite consistency
  --reference-mime-type <str>   Reference image MIME type override
  --agent-hub-fallback          Required: confirm the caller has no native
                                image generation and wants Agent Hub image
                                generation.
  --help                        Show this message and exit.
help.asset import:
Usage: st design asset import [OPTIONS] {name} {image_file}

  Import a self/user-generated image into Asset Studio for approval.

  This is the manual/current-agent path. It does not invoke Agent Hub image
  generation. Use it when the project lead chooses for you (or another
  agent/user) to create the image yourself, while still preserving the Asset
  Studio review and approval gate.

Arguments:
  name        Asset display name  [required]
  image_file  PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG image to store in Asset Studio  [required]

Options:
  --prompt <str>           Brief/source note shown with the asset  [default:
                           Manual asset import]
  -d, --description <str>  Optional description stored with the asset
  -t, --type <str>         Asset type (sprite, sprite_sheet, portrait,
                           environment, icon, illustration, ui_texture,
                           marketing_mockup, tile_set, concept_art)  [default:
                           sprite]
  -w, --workflow <str>     Workflow lane: concept, production, marketing, ui
                           [default: concept]
  --background <str>       Background mode: transparent, solid, scene
                           [default: transparent]
  --tags <str>             Comma-separated tags
  --sheet-columns <int>    Sprite sheet columns
  --sheet-rows <int>       Sprite sheet rows
  --frame-width <int>      Sprite sheet frame width
  --frame-height <int>     Sprite sheet frame height
  --animations <str>       Comma-separated animation row labels
  --source-asset-id <int>  Source asset DB id for variant derivation
  --generator-note <str>   Who/what produced this manual asset
  --help                   Show this message and exit.
help.asset critique:
Usage: st design asset critique [OPTIONS] {image_file}

  Critique a visual game asset through Agent Hub.

  This is the canonical non-siloed game-asset critique surface. It calls an
  Agent Hub specialist (`game-art-critic` by default), can run a multi-model
  panel, and returns compact structured output suitable for agent workflows.

  Examples:     st -P the-aftertimes design asset critique ranger-proof.png
  --kind sprite     st -P the-aftertimes design asset critique ranger-
  proof.png --kind sprite --gemma     st -P the-aftertimes design asset
  critique ranger-proof.png --ensemble     st design asset critique sheet.png
  -M xai/grok-4.20-0309-reasoning -M gemini-3.1-flash-lite

Arguments:
  image_file  PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP image to critique  [required]

Options:
  --brief <str>                Asset-specific art direction / acceptance
                               criteria
  --brief-file <path>          Read art direction / acceptance criteria from a
                               file
  --kind <str>                 Asset kind: sprite, animation, tileset,
                               environment, ui, icon, vfx  [default: sprite]
  --agent <str>                Agent Hub visual critique agent slug  [default:
                               game-art-critic]
  --gemma                      Use local Gemma 4 12B game-art critic agent
  -M, --model <str>            Model override. Repeat for a critique panel.
  --ensemble                   Run the default complementary critique panel
                               instead of only the agent default.
  --memory / --no-memory       Enable Agent Hub memory injection  [default:
                               memory]
  -t, --timeout <float range>  HTTP read-timeout per critique call  [default:
                               120.0; x>=1.0]
  --help                       Show this message and exit.
help.asset export:
Usage: st design asset export [OPTIONS] {asset_id}

  Export an existing Design Ops asset.

  Currently supports sprite sheet frame exports.

Arguments:
  asset_id  Design asset id to export  [required]

Options:
  -t, --type <str>  Export type (currently: sprite-frames)  [default: sprite-
                    frames]
  --help            Show this message and exit.
help.ui:
Usage: st design ui [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  UI Design mockups. `create` / `attach` store hand-authored HTML. `analyze` /
  `rerun` invoke the AI ui-mockup-designer agent.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  analyze  AI-analyze a live URL and produce a UI mockup via the design...
  rerun    Rerun a stored UI mockup through the AI design agent.
  create   Store hand-authored HTML as a new mockup (no AI regeneration).
  attach   Attach a hand-authored HTML revision to an existing mockup.
help.ui analyze:
Usage: st design ui analyze [OPTIONS] {page_url}

  AI-analyze a live URL and produce a UI mockup via the design agent.

  Requires the page to be reachable. Invokes the `ui-mockup-designer` agent
  through Agent Hub, which screenshots the page and proposes a redesign. Use
  this when you want AI-generated suggestions from a live reference.

  Use `st design ui create` instead when you (or another agent) want to hand-
  author the HTML and just have it stored without AI regeneration.

Arguments:
  page_url  Fully-qualified page URL to analyze  [required]

Options:
  --page-path <str>  Optional project page path metadata
  --help             Show this message and exit.
help.ui rerun:
Usage: st design ui rerun [OPTIONS] {mockup_id}

  Rerun a stored UI mockup through the AI design agent.

  Always invokes the `ui-mockup-designer` agent and saves the regenerated HTML
  as a child version. The agent rewrites the HTML — your exact markup will not
  survive.

  Use `st design ui attach` instead when you want to save a hand-authored
  revision under an existing mockup without AI regeneration.

Arguments:
  mockup_id  Mockup id to rerun  [required]

Options:
  -n, --notes <str>    Revision notes for the UI mockup agent
  --notes-file <path>  Path to a file containing revision notes
  --help               Show this message and exit.
help.ui create:
Usage: st design ui create [OPTIONS] {name}

  Store hand-authored HTML as a new mockup (no AI regeneration).

  Use this when you (or another agent) want to commit a specific HTML layout
  and have it appear in the project's design gallery exactly as written. The
  HTML is saved verbatim with generator="manual-html".

  Don't use this for AI-driven mockup generation — use `ui analyze` for a
  fresh AI proposal from a live URL, or `ui rerun` to revise an existing
  mockup with the AI agent.

  Examples:     st -P portfolio-ai design ui create today-layout-a \
  --html-file /tmp/layout-a.html \         --reference-url
  https://example.com/ \         --reference-image /tmp/today.png \         -d
  "Balanced /today layout: hero + digest"

      st -P portfolio-ai design ui create signal-card --html
      "<section>...</section>" \         --mockup-type component --tags
      "signals,deterministic"

Arguments:
  name  Mockup display name  [required]

Options:
  --html <str>              Inline HTML content for the mockup
  --html-file <path>        Path to a file containing the HTML mockup
  -d, --description <str>   Optional description stored with the mockup
  --mockup-type <str>       Mockup classification: page, component, layout,
                            flow, system  [default: page]
  --reference-url <str>     Live page URL this mockup references (stored as
                            page_path)
  --reference-image <path>  Path to a reference screenshot; stored in metadata
                            as reference_image_path
  --tags <str>              Comma-separated tags stored in metadata
  --task-id <str>           Optional task id to associate with the mockup
  --help                    Show this message and exit.
help.ui attach:
Usage: st design ui attach [OPTIONS] {mockup_id}

  Attach a hand-authored HTML revision to an existing mockup.

  Resolves the public mockup id (string) to its DB row id and creates a child
  mockup linked via parent_mockup_id, preserving the iteration chain in the
  gallery. The HTML is stored verbatim — no AI regeneration.

  Use `st design ui rerun` instead when you want the AI ui-mockup-designer
  agent to generate the next iteration for you.

  Example:     st -P portfolio-ai design ui attach mk-abc123 \         --html-
  file /tmp/layout-a-v2.html \         -d "Tightened spacing, added
  deterministic badge"

Arguments:
  mockup_id  Existing mockup id (e.g. mk-abc123) to attach a revision to
             [required]

Options:
  --html <str>              Inline HTML content for the revision
  --html-file <path>        Path to a file containing the revision HTML
  -d, --description <str>   Optional description stored with the revision
  --reference-url <str>     Live page URL this revision references
  --reference-image <path>  Path to a reference screenshot; stored in metadata
                            as reference_image_path
  --help                    Show this message and exit.

usage.cmd: st design ui create | st design asset import | st design asset generate
usage.when: creating UI mockups, game art, sprites, icons, tile sets, portraits, or marketing visuals
precautions: before generating visual work, ask the project lead whether the current agent/user should create it manually or Agent Hub design/image agents should generate it
use st design ui create/attach for hand-authored HTML UI mockups; never route UI screens through asset image generation
use st design asset import for current-agent/user-generated PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG assets so they still enter Asset Studio approval
use st design asset critique for Agent Hub-routed visual/design critique before accepting production game assets
use the calling agent's native image generator first, then st design asset import; use st design asset generate only as an explicit Agent Hub fallback when the caller has no native image generation
Design Ops storage is durable project state; never configure Asset Studio or UI mockup storage under /tmp
do not export or commit visual assets into the repo until approved in Design/Asset Studio
